payload: {"note": "d10 Thu 07:29: dish_rack_k1 holds pot_1; Leo present. Confirms dish_rack_k1 as static hub for pot_1 (P~0.90). Absence of pan_1/mugs/water_bottles lowers their priors here. Prioritize counter_k1 for mugs/water_bottles, not dish_rack_k1.", "fork": {"beliefs": "The household operates on a strict 'personal territory' model. Each resident (Mara, Leo, Sofia) has a designated bedroom (bedroom_1, bedroom_2, bedroom_3 respectively) and a corresponding desk (desk_b1, desk_b2, desk_b3). Personal items (backpacks, laptops, phones, wallets, keys, mugs, notebooks, jackets, umbrellas, water bottles, chargers, gaming controllers, headphones, glasses, hairbrushes, makeup kits, medication bottles, lunchboxes) are almost exclusively found in the owner's bedroom or on the owner's person. Shared spaces (living, kitchen, entry) contain only communal items (blanket_1, remote_1, vacuum_cleaner_1, plates, bowls, pans, pots, laundry_basket_1) or items temporarily moved for immediate use. Why: This is the most common household organization pattern; it minimizes search space by mapping object ownership to specific rooms. Evidence: None yet, but this is the baseline assumption for a new installation. If an object is missing from its owner's bedroom, it is likely ON_PERSON or OUT_OF_HOUSE. If a personal item is found in a shared space, it is an anomaly or temporary state. The entry area (entry_table_e1, entry_hook_e1) is the primary drop zone for keys, wallets, and jackets upon arrival/departure. The kitchen counter (counter_k1) is the primary drop zone for mugs, water bottles, and phones during meal times. The living room (coffee_table_l1, tv_stand_l1) is the primary drop zone for remotes, controllers, and books during leisure time. Bedroom floors (bedroom_floor_b1, bedroom_floor_b2, bedroom_floor_b3) are the primary drop zone for jackets, backpacks, and shoes upon entering the bedroom. Nightstands (nightstand_b1, nightstand_b2, nightstand_b3) are the primary drop zone for phones, glasses, and chargers at night. Desks (desk_b1, desk_b2, desk_b3) are the primary drop zone for laptops, notebooks, pens, and chargers during work/study. Beds (bed_b1, bed_b2, bed_b3) are not drop zones for personal items (P~0.05). dish_rack_k1 is a static hub for pot_1 (P~0.90) but not for mugs/water_bottles/pan_1. sink_k1 is a drop zone for mugs (mug_mara P~0.40) and wallets (wallet_leo P~0.30). desk_b2 is not a static drop zone for Leo's items (P~0.05). desk_b3 is static storage for Sofia's grooming items (P~0.80). counter_k1 is a high-probability (P~0.80) static hub for multi-resident personal items (backpacks, mugs, phones, water bottles) during mornings.", "why": "Updated beliefs to reflect that dish_rack_k1 is a static hub for pot_1 but not for other kitchen items, and to consolidate previous observations about counter_k1, desk_b2, and desk_b3."}}
